root_idea.summary: The root centers on making a notch, opening, or perforation, and extends to the ruination or loss of a built or inhabited state.
root_idea.development: The lexical development connects piercing and perforation with ruin as the opposite of flourishing or habitation; the sense of a camel-thief is explained as making a breach in another's property. Several specialized bird, plant, and anatomical usages remain distinct branches.

senses.definition: To bring a house, dwelling, or other inhabited place to ruin; to lay waste or demolish it.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic construction يُخْرِبُونَ بُيُوتَهُمْ, this is the destructive interpretation of what was done to the houses.

senses.definition: To leave or evacuate a house, leaving it uninhabited or in a state of ruin.
senses.usage_conditions: This is a reported Quranic interpretation of يُخْرِبُونَ بُيُوتَهُمْ, emphasizing departure or evacuation rather than the act of demolition itself.

senses.definition: Ruin, destruction, or waste of a place or building; the condition opposite to flourishing and habitation.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic expression خَرَابِهَا, it denotes the ruining or destruction of the mosques.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become ruined, waste, uninhabited, depopulated, deserted, desolate, or uncultivated; said of a place, country, dwelling, or house.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive Form I verb describing the state or becoming of a place.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To have a slit or round perforation; of an ear, to be slit or pierced.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A distinct Form I use describing a perforated object or ear.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To steal, especially to steal another person's camels; to become a thief or robber.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The camel-stealing construction is explicitly attested alongside the broader sense of becoming a thief.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To bore, perforate, or slit a thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive Form I use applied to an object that is pierced or opened.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause entrusted deposits to be lost or to perish.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional figurative expression describes deposits entrusted to someone as becoming lost with him.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become demolished or ruined.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Said of a building or structure; this is a Form V inchoative or middle construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become perforated with many holes or become full of holes.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Said especially of a skin used for water or milk.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become broken by misfortune.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use reported as such in the lexical evidence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To lament for an event or circumstance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested in the construction اِسْتَخْرَبْتُ لِهٰذَا الأَمْرِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be angry with someone, especially after separation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative construction directed toward a person who has separated himself from the speaker.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To yearn toward, long for, or desire someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A distinct figurative interpretation of اِسْتَخْرَبَ إِلَيْهِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a canker-worm to corrode a tree.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The form is treated by some authorities as radically quadriliteral.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The place where an elevated accumulation of sand terminates, producing trees of the kind called غَضًا.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A topographical noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The male of the bustard called حُبَارَى; in some usage, the bustard generally.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural خِرْبَانٌ is also attested for this bird sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Cowardly; a coward.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative adjective or substantive use distinct from the bird name.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Ruined, waste, uninhabited, depopulated, deserted, desolate, or uncultivated.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjective applied to a place, country, dwelling, or place of abode.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Without marrow in the bone; figuratively, unsafe to trust or unreliable in keeping an entrusted matter.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: These are figurative applications of the adjective.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A hole, perforation, or bore, whether round or otherwise; including an ear hole, the eye of a needle, and certain bodily openings.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word can denote a perforation generally and is also used for specifically named openings; the cited bodily applications do not impose a general object restriction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The socket of the hip where the head of the thigh-bone is inserted; the plural may also denote the lower extremities of the shoulder-blades.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical sense distinct from the general meaning of a hole or perforation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The loop of a leather water-bag by which it is suspended.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The sense is associated with the loop's round form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A vice, fault, moral or religious unsoundness, disgraceful act, crime, or bad word or saying.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A moral and social evaluation, including a quality that induces suspicion or evil opinion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A trial or affliction.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A distinct abstract use of the noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In the expression فَارٌّ بِخُرْبَةٍ, property carried away by a fugitive who intends unlawfully to appropriate it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional idiom describing flight with something for the purpose of taking possession of it unlawfully.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A state or condition of disgrace or shame; a shameful or disgraceful act.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word may denote either the condition of one characterized by disgrace or a single act of that kind.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Baseness, vileness, disgrace, ignominy, or contemptibleness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A moral and social sense distinct from physical ruin.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The part or parts of the body that are indecent to expose.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical and modesty-related term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A kind of tree or plant, especially the carob or locust-tree; the name may also cover related wild or Syrian varieties.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A botanical collective noun with several described varieties.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A stealer of camels; by extension, a thief or robber.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The camel-stealing sense is treated as primary in the lexical evidence, with the broader sense extended from it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having a slit, pierced, or perforated ear.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjective applied to a person or animal with an ear that has been slit or bored; the examples do not restrict the sense to a particular class of bearer.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An empty bee-hive from which honey has not been collected.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested in the phrase خَلِيَّةٌ مُخْرِبَةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A hole or cell like those of hornets' nests; specifically a wax cell in which bees deposit honey.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A singular associated with the plural نَخَارِيبُ.

lane_unit_coverage.note: The ear-hole width is covered by the general perforation sense.
The needle-eye and bodily-opening applications are stated in the broader hole sense.
The verbal-noun statement is covered by the Quranic noun's ruin sense.
Infinitival and synonymous usage adds no separate lexical branch.
The listed bearers and ear conditions are covered by the general ear-perforation adjective.

cautions: For 59:2, the evidence records both a destructive interpretation and an interpretation involving departure or evacuation; both are retained as Quranic senses. It also records an alternate Form II reading, while the public form follows QAC's Form IV identity.
